title: Deeper dive: Were Touch Bar’s problems software rather than hardware? – Unsung
excerpt: A blog about software craft and quality
content_html:
The Touch Bar arrived in 2016 seemingly already pre-doomed, on a generation of machines that had a “we’ve run out of ideas” smell all around them. The arrow keys were reshaped, the keyboard got a slimming down, and even the beloved MagSafe wasn’t, in fact, safe. All of these changes would prove unpopular and get reverted in time, and the axe would eventually come for the Touch Bar, too.

With an enormous benefit of hindsight, a decade after its arrival, and on the (rumored) eve of fully multitouch MacBooks, I wanted to look critically at the Touch Bar in more detail. I put a spicy title above this post, and while I’m not sure I can answer it in the affirmative, I feel I got surprisingly close to that.

What did the Touch Bar do?

The Touch Bar replaced the top row of the keyboard with a narrow touch screen and a Touch ID surface/​button on the right.

The touch screen provided a constant virtual Esc key on the left, and the remainder could become one of a few things:

  • app controls – whatever the app wanted (either buttons or more interactive surfaces):
  • control strip – roughly the same as what function keys do today by default (brightness, transport controls, volume):
  • a hybrid mode of smaller app controls on the left, and expandable control strip on the right:
  • F1–F12 keys:
  • a few smaller modes, like showing spaces, quick actions, or emoji:
  • small submodes where only the middle of the Touch Bar would be taken over:

The Verge has a five-minute video that shows a lot of this stuff nicely.

Functionality

Touch Bar arrived with a hybrid of functionality for casual and pro users – some built into the macOS itself, and some coming from specific Apple-owned apps.

A few apps offered basically a subset of their toolbars (although often without customization), with an occasional submenu, like digging deeper into font options or choosing a color adjustment. Some apps like Safari and Photo would invest in tiny previews of objects.

Particularly demo-friendly were sliders for volume and brightness, and those in specific apps – playback in QuickTime, or swiping through the photo gallery, clearly inspired by similar controls on the iPhone. Even though Touch Bar was referred to as “multitouch,” it really only supported tapping and horizontal swiping, with just the latter being something classic function keys clearly couldn’t do.

A simple but effective was also an arrow pointing to Touch ID authorization and payments – a small example of software proprioception – which Apple even included as a GIF in their press release:

But there were also some strange moments, the strategy feeling a bit like “let’s throw a lot of stuff at this and see what sticks” (then again, it worked for the first Apple Watch!):

  • Any system dialog would show its buttons repeated in the Touch Bar. This felt puzzling to me, as those were already served well by both mouse interactions and keyboard (Esc/Enter).
  • It was nice that you could drag the volume or brightness control, but then the slider would be disconnected from your finger and the volume would also appear in the old HUD on the screen, altogether feeling like different parts of the system weren’t aware of each other.
  • Xcode offered a button to comment out the current line or selection, which must have felt almost insulting to programmers – is there anyone who’d prefer that over the ⌘/ key combination?

Lastly, for the first edition, the IA felt complex:

  • Word completion was in the middle of the bar, but the emoji entry point was on the left.
  • There were many kinds of chevrons (at least three!), and the action didn’t fully match their arrows – some of the chevrons indeed made the controls expand in an expected direction, but some instead drilled deeper and took half of the bar, and others took over the whole thing. (On top of that, some controls had regular horizontal scrolling.)
  • Some controls that looked like regular buttons expanded on tap, too, so in effect it was never truly clear what a control would do when touched.
  • The close boxes were sometimes on the left, and sometimes on the right of the buttons.
Settings

Strangely for such a high-profile feature, the Touch Bar settings arrived sprinkled in between older keyboard options, rather than in a separate Touch Bar tab that could help you understand the whole system easier, and also perhaps offer nice previews of what was possible.

Apple’s penchant to brand even small things also backfired a little bit – customizing the Touch Bar required facing strange phrases like Quick Actions, App Controls, and Control Strip (this is where the usually non-nostalgic Apple reused a classic name, rather than naming it System Controls to mirror App Controls).

On the other hand, the Customize Control Strip interaction here was an absolute highlight, providing a magical-feeling bridge between the world of the Touch Bar and the heavens above it – this was perhaps the best-designed part of the whole system:

(That kind of customization was also available in some, but not all of the apps that supported the Touch Bar.)

By the way, Apple seems to have learned the settings lesson since 2016, or even overlearned; the action button introduced to the iPhone in 2023 came with a lavish new interface:

First public reactions and the evolution

Back in 2016, the Touch Bar arrived to muted optimism (“not great, perhaps promising, looking forward to season two and three”), mixed with loud frustration from seemingly every single person who relied on the physical Esc key.

Touch Bar was only revisited once, in 2019; this slight update reintroduced a mechanical Esc key, and felt slightly faster in use.

There were no other hardware improvements, and I believe zero software changes from Apple’s side during the whole lifetime of the feature. Some third-party apps added Touch Bar support in the first few years, but even then the verdict seemed somewhat reserved:

Most Final Cut Pro power users will be so used to using keyboard shortcuts for the editing functions they use regularly that they may not find the Touch Bar any quicker for simple editing and playback, but the sheer number of context-dependent settings means it’s likely to prove its value eventually.

The Touch Bar never made it to non-Pro MacBooks or other computers, and started being phased out altogether five years after its arrival. Perplexingly and for reasons we might never know, the project was “maintenanced” almost as soon as it launched, and it wasn’t immediately removed perhaps only to save face.

Haptics and ergonomics

Touch Bar felt unpleasant to fingers.

People’s ire around the Esc key was mostly in how “dead” it felt next to the other keys, which was especially important for something further in the periphery, used as an escape hatch or as a core interaction by programmers. (The key was also slightly offset, likely only to preserve symmetry vis-à-vis Touch ID on the other side.)

I bet that the unavoidable and constant comparison of the feel of the Touch Bar buttons to the real keys just below was what made the whole thing feel worse than it was, and I’ve always wondered if haptics could have helped here. What if a light touch offered gentle haptic feedback similar to feeling the “ridges” of the keys without pressing them, and a deeper press offered a proper haptic tap?

Already in 2016, Apple had similar tech in the trackpad underneath. I bet I’m underestimating how hard or expensive it would be to repurpose it, but: the iPods never had true haptic feedback, yet even in the first model they arrived with a little speaker that emitted haptic-like sounds on actions. It was surprisingly effective, and I was curious why Apple didn’t do the same thing here.

On top of that, while the row of function keys above is fun for an occasional press, it doesn’t ergonomically seem as great in prolonged use. Reaching up to the Touch Bar is more effort than reaching for the trackpad, whether you put it below or to the side – there’s a reason keyboards grow wider but they rarely grow taller. In The Verge video above, you can see the reviewer use a Touch Bar button as a modifier key while interacting with the trackpad below, and it feels unpleasant just watching that happen:

On top of that, the Touch Bar surface sat lower than the surface of the keys, which made it ever so slightly less pleasant to use – it didn’t only feel like it was above the keys, but also behind them.

There were other rough edges that added up:

  • The Touch Bar would go to sleep eagerly (after only 60+15 seconds), hiding all its controls and forcing you to tap it or press a key to wake it up.
  • The quality of the animations was not the same as on the other touch devices or the Apple TV.
  • While the Touch Bar itself was fast enough to support smooth scrolling, there was also some (I think intentional) delay when pressing the Fn key and some Touch Bar controls, plus a general slight, but perceivable latency on every touch.
  • Speaking of scrolling, it was uneven: in Calendar, you could use momentum scrolling but the calendar didn’t update in real time, and stopping the momentum by tapping anywhere like on the iPhone actually selected a different month:
  • Often the only way to escape a submode was to press a close box on the left, which was unpleasant given the position of your hand; there was no thoughtful shortcut, like double tapping an option, to exit faster.
Size

Using the Touch Bar was being constantly aware of its small size: The previews were tiny, your fingers overlapped content all the time, and scrolling only happened in the horizontal plane. (And you had to keep your finger in a straight line instead of a slight arc – not a natural gesture.)

Expanding the Control Strip required tapping on a very small chevron; there were tons of those tiny chevrons elsewhere, too, narrow and hard to press without haptic feedback. It made the interface feel fiddly, a strange compromise from a company that thoughtfully established and enforced the “44 pixels” minimum size for touch targets with the first iPhone. (The chevrons were exactly half of the recommended minimal physical width of any touch target on the 2007 iPhone – 3.5mm instead of 7mm.)

Many spaces felt tight in other ways, too. Craig Federighi’s keynote demo showing Safari previews was claustrophobic with just five tabs:

When using any typing surface, the Touch Bar would get divided into three areas: app controls, suggested words, and control strip on the right:

In other apps, some areas were scrollable, but there was no room for a scrollbar. Using the Touch Bar in any meaningful capacity felt like constantly guessing what’s movable and what isn’t, and constantly resizing tiny virtual windows, except without any pleasant resizing mechanics from Apple’s larger screens. Here, the emoji pane UI is doing some really clever things to help traverse hundreds of emoji, yet it still feels not enough:

The interactions in photo editing and a few other places felt so cramped and convoluted that I wonder why anyone would choose them over the spaciousness and precision of the screen above.

I wonder if the limited height also created other downstream effects. For example, drilling down did a (slow) fadeout/​fade in effect, instead of scrolling down and up to help you understand the hierarchy – and showing the chevron pointing in that direction, too. I am guessing that was because the movement would suggest you can swipe up and down, and there simply wasn’t enough room for that gesture to feel good.

Using the Touch Bar, I kept thinking of the wonderful customization feature I mentioned that cleverly fused the Touch Bar with the screen above, and also a similar interaction from a 1980s Xerox machine (where pressing the key below More would show other options):

Could this have worked for other Touch Bar interactions to create more room, or would it become frustrating as your fingers would naturally want to tap the bottom of the screen? There is a small thoughtful integration like this in text editing, where the Touch Bar seems to be aware that while your fingers are downstairs, you might be looking up:

But then, in the same place, choosing a color is not integrated the same way:

All in all, the Touch Bar was new I/O sandwiched between an old O and an even older I, and it didn’t seem like all the relationships here were fully figured out.

Could Touch Bar just grow larger? Asus Zenbook Pro showed the endgame of this idea – it enabled some new interesting things, but threw in tons of more challenges like a missing trackpad, or deciding what to put on each surface:

I wouldn’t expect Touch Bar to go nearly as far, but I was curious to see it grow a little bit vertically to alleviate some of the pains.

Customization and infrastructure

Apple bet the Touch Bar house on individual app built-in support and a few core interactions. But I wonder in hindsight if the answer was user customization.

On that front, the Touch Bar exposed Apple’s underinvestment in the actions infrastructure. Keyboard customization in macOS has already felt ancient in 2016 and did not improve since, and Shortcuts app didn’t even exist then. This was Apple’s chance to provide a gentler Keyboard Maestro-like experience for the masses, but the Touch Bar didn’t allow you to plop in even a few function keys alongside the new features – the only option for that was the old-fashioned mode with F1–F12 with none of the benefits of the Touch Bar (you couldn’t even change the labels!), and also without haptics.

Sure, there was a gesture in this direction with Quick Actions, but those felt extremely underbaked; in my explorations with Automator and Touch Bar, I encountered some truly confusing settings and flows and could never make it work fully. Here, I had to go to a faraway System Preferences pane, and see various Quick Actions that were not talking to one another:

In a better setup, it would be possible to assign any key or action or menu command to any ground-floor Touch Bar button; something like SF Symbols (formalized in 2019) could provide all the necessary icons. Or, one could imagine some delightful integrated interactions like this one that would make it easy and pleasant to make the Touch Bar feel personally useful.

Or, how about sparklines or other tiny widgets that’d quickly show visual status, of the kind pro users like to put in the menu bar already, and easily pluggable to data sources (see the very recent TerminalWidget)? Or a left/​right slide gesture, buttons, or a keyboard combination to swap between Touch Bar “spaces”?

How about learning what commands you use most often that don’t have keyboard shortcuts, per app, and suggesting them as the first five buttons on the Touch Bar?

Could the Touch Bar have been saved?

Today, it often feels like the Touch Bar chose revolution in the moments the right answer was evolution, and evolution in places that called for a revolution. With hindsight, after seeing projects like Stream Deck and Flux Keyboard capture people’s attention, maybe it could have worked this way:

  • First version arrives with a physical Esc or at least “sound-based haptics,” and allows you to do more things via much nicer settings software: easy assigning of buttons to system actions, and icons so you no longer have to remember whether it was F3 or F7 doing your thing. Don’t treat the Touch Bar as repudiation of function keys, but as their enhancement. On top of that, add some easy-to-put-together widgetlets and sparklines. This is Pro hardware, and these feel like pro features.
  • Staying tighter, focused, and reigning in some more complex interactions would help, too (problem: they look so good in videos!). Instead of boiling the ocean and recreating a lot of the existing GUI in a cramped space, focus on just one–two great interactions per app. Finder: Show the Quick Actions that were already customizable and not as easy to access in some views! Emoji: Paginate instead of scroll, but do a really clever pagination that highlights the power of a parallax swipe gesture that can only exist here. System: Add immediate screenshotting by default.
  • If this worked, subsequent versions would add haptics, perhaps increase the size, and go mainstream from pro users to regular users, learning all the useful lessons along the way (also from third-party apps like Pock).

But I’m not sure. Touch is fun but there is, ultimately, a ceiling on value you can squeeze out of a small touch strip, and a floor on complexity of yet another input/​output device.

And there was always an elephant in the hardware room – many pro users are likely to use computers on desks with separate keyboards, which puts the Touch Bar either too far away or makes it altogether inaccessible. In the decade since, Apple hasn’t even solved this for Touch ID, the only part of the Touch Bar that didn’t get sacrificed to the angry IBM 3270 terminal gods.

Would the Touch Bar have worked as a standalone device? Could it ever become good enough for you to want to pay for it twice?

Perhaps not. But had Apple improved the keyboard and action customization software for the Touch Bar, only to see it crash and burn, we could at least still keep the software.

sentences.en: Some controls that looked like regular buttons expanded on tap, too, so in effect it was never truly clear what a control would do when touched.

sentences.en: Strangely for such a high-profile feature, the Touch Bar settings arrived sprinkled in between older keyboard options, rather than in a separate Touch Bar tab that could help you understand the whole system easier, and also perhaps offer nice previews of what was possible.

blocks.html_en:
Back in 2016, the Touch Bar arrived to muted optimism (“not great, perhaps promising, looking forward to season two and three”), mixed with loud frustration from seemingly every single person who relied on the physical Esc key.

Touch Bar was only revisited once, in 2019; this slight update reintroduced a mechanical Esc key, and felt slightly faster in use.

sentences.en: Back in 2016, the Touch Bar arrived to muted optimism (“not great, perhaps promising, looking forward to season two and three”), mixed with loud frustration from seemingly every single person who relied on the physical Esc key.

sentences.zh: Touch Bar 只在 2019 年被重新审视过一次；这次轻微的更新重新引入了机械 Esc 键，使用起来感觉稍快一些。

sentences.en: What if a light touch offered gentle haptic feedback similar to feeling the “ridges” of the keys without pressing them, and a deeper press offered a proper haptic tap?

blocks.html_en: • The Touch Bar would go to sleep eagerly (after only 60+15 seconds), hiding all its controls and forcing you to tap it or press a key to wake it up.

sentences.en: The Touch Bar would go to sleep eagerly (after only 60+15 seconds), hiding all its controls and forcing you to tap it or press a key to wake it up.
sentences.zh: Touch Bar 会急切地进入睡眠状态（仅 60+15 秒后），隐藏其所有控件并迫使您点击它或按某个键将其唤醒。

blocks.html_en: • The quality of the animations was not the same as on the other touch devices or the Apple TV.

sentences.en: The quality of the animations was not the same as on the other touch devices or the Apple TV.
sentences.zh: 动画的质量与其他触摸设备或 Apple TV 上的不同。

blocks.html_en: • While the Touch Bar itself was fast enough to support smooth scrolling, there was also some (I think intentional) delay when pressing the Fn key and some Touch Bar controls, plus a general slight, but perceivable latency on every touch.

sentences.en: While the Touch Bar itself was fast enough to support smooth scrolling, there was also some (I think intentional) delay when pressing the Fn key and some Touch Bar controls, plus a general slight, but perceivable latency on every touch.
sentences.zh: 虽然 Touch Bar 本身的速度足以支持平滑滚动，但按下 Fn 键和某些 Touch Bar 控件时也会出现一些（我认为是故意的）延迟，而且每次触摸时都会出现轻微但可察觉的延迟。

blocks.html_en: • Speaking of scrolling, it was uneven: in Calendar, you could use momentum scrolling but the calendar didn’t update in real time, and stopping the momentum by tapping anywhere like on the iPhone actually selected a different month:

sentences.en: Speaking of scrolling, it was uneven: in Calendar, you could use momentum scrolling but the calendar didn’t update in real time, and stopping the momentum by tapping anywhere like on the iPhone actually selected a different month:
sentences.zh: 说到滚动，它是不平衡的：在日历中，你可以使用动量滚动，但日历不会实时更新，并且通过点击任意位置来停止动量，就像在 iPhone 上实际上选择了不同的月份一样：

blocks.html_en: • Often the only way to escape a submode was to press a close box on the left, which was unpleasant given the position of your hand; there was no thoughtful shortcut, like double tapping an option, to exit faster.

sentences.en: Often the only way to escape a submode was to press a close box on the left, which was unpleasant given the position of your hand; there was no thoughtful shortcut, like double tapping an option, to exit faster.
sentences.zh: 通常，退出子模式的唯一方法是按左侧的关闭框，考虑到你手的位置，这很不愉快；没有深思熟虑的捷径，比如双击一个选项，可以更快地退出。

blocks.html_en: Size

Using the Touch Bar was being constantly aware of its small size: The previews were tiny, your fingers overlapped content all the time, and scrolling only happened in the horizontal plane. (And you had to keep your finger in a straight line instead of a slight arc – not a natural gesture.)

sentences.en: Using the Touch Bar was being constantly aware of its small size: The previews were tiny, your fingers overlapped content all the time, and scrolling only happened in the horizontal plane.
sentences.zh: 使用 Touch Bar 时要不断意识到它的小尺寸：预览很小，手指始终与内容重叠，并且滚动仅发生在水平面上。

sentences.en: (And you had to keep your finger in a straight line instead of a slight arc – not a natural gesture.)
sentences.zh: （而且你的手指必须保持在一条直线上，而不是轻微的弧线——这不是一个自然的手势。）

blocks.html_en: Expanding the Control Strip required tapping on a very small chevron; there were tons of those tiny chevrons elsewhere, too, narrow and hard to press without haptic feedback. It made the interface feel fiddly, a strange compromise from a company that thoughtfully established and enforced the “44 pixels” minimum size for touch targets with the first iPhone. (The chevrons were exactly half of the recommended minimal physical width of any touch target on the 2007 iPhone – 3.5mm instead of 7mm.)

sentences.en: Expanding the Control Strip required tapping on a very small chevron; there were tons of those tiny chevrons elsewhere, too, narrow and hard to press without haptic feedback.
sentences.zh: 扩展控制条需要点击一个非常小的 V 形；其他地方也有大量这样的小 V 形图案，它们很窄，如果没有触觉反馈，很难按下。

sentences.en: It made the interface feel fiddly, a strange compromise from a company that thoughtfully established and enforced the “44 pixels” minimum size for touch targets with the first iPhone.
sentences.zh: 它让界面感觉很繁琐，这是一家公司的奇怪妥协，该公司在第一代 iPhone 上深思熟虑地制定并强制执行了“44 像素”最小触摸目标尺寸。

sentences.en: (The chevrons were exactly half of the recommended minimal physical width of any touch target on the 2007 iPhone – 3.5mm instead of 7mm.)
sentences.zh: （V 形图案正好是 2007 年 iPhone 上任何触摸目标建议最小物理宽度的一半——3.5 毫米，而不是 7 毫米。）

blocks.html_en: Many spaces felt tight in other ways, too. Craig Federighi’s keynote demo showing Safari previews was claustrophobic with just five tabs:

sentences.en: Many spaces felt tight in other ways, too.
sentences.zh: 许多空间在其他方面也感觉紧张。

sentences.en: Craig Federighi’s keynote demo showing Safari previews was claustrophobic with just five tabs:
sentences.zh: Craig Federighi 的主题演示展示了 Safari 预览，只有五个选项卡，让人感到幽闭恐怖：

blocks.html_en: When using any typing surface, the Touch Bar would get divided into three areas: app controls, suggested words, and control strip on the right:

sentences.en: When using any typing surface, the Touch Bar would get divided into three areas: app controls, suggested words, and control strip on the right:
sentences.zh: 使用任何打字表面时，触摸栏将分为三个区域：应用程序控件、建议单词和右侧的控制条：

blocks.html_en: In other apps, some areas were scrollable, but there was no room for a scrollbar. Using the Touch Bar in any meaningful capacity felt like constantly guessing what’s movable and what isn’t, and constantly resizing tiny virtual windows, except without any pleasant resizing mechanics from Apple’s larger screens. Here, the emoji pane UI is doing some really clever things to help traverse hundreds of emoji, yet it still feels not enough:

sentences.en: In other apps, some areas were scrollable, but there was no room for a scrollbar.
sentences.zh: 在其他应用程序中，某些区域是可滚动的，但没有空间放置滚动条。

sentences.en: Using the Touch Bar in any meaningful capacity felt like constantly guessing what’s movable and what isn’t, and constantly resizing tiny virtual windows, except without any pleasant resizing mechanics from Apple’s larger screens.
sentences.zh: 以任何有意义的方式使用 Touch Bar 感觉就像不断猜测什么是可移动的、什么是不可移动的，并不断调整微小的虚拟窗口的大小，除了苹果大屏幕没有任何令人愉快的调整大小机制。

sentences.en: Here, the emoji pane UI is doing some really clever things to help traverse hundreds of emoji, yet it still feels not enough:
sentences.zh: 在这里，表情符号窗格 UI 正在做一些非常聪明的事情来帮助遍历数百个表情符号，但它仍然感觉不够：

blocks.html_en: The interactions in photo editing and a few other places felt so cramped and convoluted that I wonder why anyone would choose them over the spaciousness and precision of the screen above.

sentences.en: The interactions in photo editing and a few other places felt so cramped and convoluted that I wonder why anyone would choose them over the spaciousness and precision of the screen above.
sentences.zh: 照片编辑和其他一些地方的交互感觉如此狭窄和复杂，我想知道为什么有人会选择它们而不是上面屏幕的宽敞和精确。

blocks.html_en: I wonder if the limited height also created other downstream effects. For example, drilling down did a (slow) fadeout/​fade in effect, instead of scrolling down and up to help you understand the hierarchy – and showing the chevron pointing in that direction, too. I am guessing that was because the movement would suggest you can swipe up and down, and there simply wasn’t enough room for that gesture to feel good.

sentences.en: I wonder if the limited height also created other downstream effects.
sentences.zh: 我想知道有限的高度是否还会产生其他下游影响。

sentences.en: For example, drilling down did a (slow) fadeout/​fade in effect, instead of scrolling down and up to help you understand the hierarchy – and showing the chevron pointing in that direction, too.
sentences.zh: 例如，向下钻取会产生（缓慢的）淡出/淡出效果，而不是向下和向上滚动来帮助您理解层次结构 - 并显示 V 形符号也指向该方向。

sentences.en: I am guessing that was because the movement would suggest you can swipe up and down, and there simply wasn’t enough room for that gesture to feel good.
sentences.zh: 我猜这是因为这个动作会建议你可以上下滑动，但根本没有足够的空间让这个手势感觉良好。

blocks.html_en: Using the Touch Bar, I kept thinking of the wonderful customization feature I mentioned that cleverly fused the Touch Bar with the screen above, and also a similar interaction from a 1980s Xerox machine (where pressing the key below More would show other options):

sentences.en: Using the Touch Bar, I kept thinking of the wonderful customization feature I mentioned that cleverly fused the Touch Bar with the screen above, and also a similar interaction from a 1980s Xerox machine (where pressing the key below More would show other options):
sentences.zh: 使用 Touch Bar，我不断想起我提到的美妙的自定义功能，该功能巧妙地将 Touch Bar 与上面的屏幕融合在一起，以及 20 世纪 80 年代 Xerox 机器的类似交互（按下面的“更多”键会显示其他选项）：

blocks.html_en: Could this have worked for other Touch Bar interactions to create more room, or would it become frustrating as your fingers would naturally want to tap the bottom of the screen? There is a small thoughtful integration like this in text editing, where the Touch Bar seems to be aware that while your fingers are downstairs, you might be looking up:

sentences.en: Could this have worked for other Touch Bar interactions to create more room, or would it become frustrating as your fingers would naturally want to tap the bottom of the screen?
sentences.zh: 这是否适用于其他 Touch Bar 交互以创造更多空间，还是会因为您的手指自然地想要点击屏幕底部而变得令人沮丧？

sentences.en: There is a small thoughtful integration like this in text editing, where the Touch Bar seems to be aware that while your fingers are downstairs, you might be looking up:
sentences.zh: 在文本编辑中，有一个像这样深思熟虑的小集成，触摸栏似乎意识到，当你的手指在楼下时，你可能正在向上看：

blocks.html_en: But then, in the same place, choosing a color is not integrated the same way:

sentences.en: But then, in the same place, choosing a color is not integrated the same way:
sentences.zh: 但是，在同一个地方，选择颜色的集成方式并不相同：

blocks.html_en: All in all, the Touch Bar was new I/O sandwiched between an old O and an even older I, and it didn’t seem like all the relationships here were fully figured out.

sentences.en: All in all, the Touch Bar was new I/O sandwiched between an old O and an even older I, and it didn’t seem like all the relationships here were fully figured out.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，Touch Bar 是一个夹在旧 O 和更旧 I 之间的新 I/O，而且似乎这里的所有关系都没有完全弄清楚。

blocks.html_en: Could Touch Bar just grow larger? Asus Zenbook Pro showed the endgame of this idea – it enabled some new interesting things, but threw in tons of more challenges like a missing trackpad, or deciding what to put on each surface:

sentences.en: Could Touch Bar just grow larger?
sentences.zh: Touch Bar 会变得更大吗？

sentences.en: Asus Zenbook Pro showed the endgame of this idea – it enabled some new interesting things, but threw in tons of more challenges like a missing trackpad, or deciding what to put on each surface:
sentences.zh: 华硕 Zenbook Pro 展示了这个想法的最终结果——它实现了一些新的有趣的事情，但也带来了更多的挑战，比如缺少触控板，或者决定在每个表面上放置什么：

blocks.html_en: I wouldn’t expect Touch Bar to go nearly as far, but I was curious to see it grow a little bit vertically to alleviate some of the pains.

sentences.en: I wouldn’t expect Touch Bar to go nearly as far, but I was curious to see it grow a little bit vertically to alleviate some of the pains.
sentences.zh: 我没想到 Touch Bar 会走得那么远，但我很好奇它会垂直增长一点，以减轻一些痛苦。

blocks.html_en: Customization and infrastructure

sentences.en: Customization and infrastructure
sentences.zh: 定制和基础设施

blocks.html_en: Apple bet the Touch Bar house on individual app built-in support and a few core interactions. But I wonder in hindsight if the answer was user customization.

sentences.en: Apple bet the Touch Bar house on individual app built-in support and a few core interactions.
sentences.zh: 苹果将​​ Touch Bar 的赌注押在了单个应用程序的内置支持和一些核心交互上。

sentences.en: But I wonder in hindsight if the answer was user customization.
sentences.zh: 但事后我想知道答案是否是用户定制。

blocks.html_en: On that front, the Touch Bar exposed Apple’s underinvestment in the actions infrastructure. Keyboard customization in macOS has already felt ancient in 2016 and did not improve since, and Shortcuts app didn’t even exist then. This was Apple’s chance to provide a gentler Keyboard Maestro-like experience for the masses, but the Touch Bar didn’t allow you to plop in even a few function keys alongside the new features – the only option for that was the old-fashioned mode with F1–F12 with none of the benefits of the Touch Bar (you couldn’t even change the labels!), and also without haptics.

sentences.en: On that front, the Touch Bar exposed Apple’s underinvestment in the actions infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，Touch Bar 暴露了苹果在操作基础设施方面投资不足。

sentences.en: Keyboard customization in macOS has already felt ancient in 2016 and did not improve since, and Shortcuts app didn’t even exist then.
sentences.zh: macOS 中的键盘自定义在 2016 年就已经显得过时了，此后就没有改进，而且当时甚至还不存在快捷方式应用程序。

sentences.en: This was Apple’s chance to provide a gentler Keyboard Maestro-like experience for the masses, but the Touch Bar didn’t allow you to plop in even a few function keys alongside the new features – the only option for that was the old-fashioned mode with F1–F12 with none of the benefits of the Touch Bar (you couldn’t even change the labels!), and also without haptics.
sentences.zh: 这是苹果为大众提供更温和的键盘大师般的体验的机会，但 Touch Bar 不允许你在新功能旁边插入哪怕几个功能键 - 唯一的选择是 F1-F12 的老式模式，没有 Touch Bar 的任何好处（你甚至无法更改标签！），也没有触觉。

blocks.html_en: Sure, there was a gesture in this direction with Quick Actions, but those felt extremely underbaked; in my explorations with Automator and Touch Bar, I encountered some truly confusing settings and flows and could never make it work fully. Here, I had to go to a faraway System Preferences pane, and see various Quick Actions that were not talking to one another:

sentences.en: Sure, there was a gesture in this direction with Quick Actions, but those felt extremely underbaked; in my explorations with Automator and Touch Bar, I encountered some truly confusing settings and flows and could never make it work fully.
sentences.zh: 当然，快速行动在这个方向上有一个手势，但那些感觉非常不成熟；在我对 Automator 和 Touch Bar 的探索中，我遇到了一些真正令人困惑的设置和流程，并且永远无法使其完全正常工作。

sentences.en: Here, I had to go to a faraway System Preferences pane, and see various Quick Actions that were not talking to one another:
sentences.zh: 在这里，我必须转到一个遥远的“系统偏好设置”窗格，并查看各种不互相通信的快速操作：

blocks.html_en: In a better setup, it would be possible to assign any key or action or menu command to any ground-floor Touch Bar button; something like SF Symbols (formalized in 2019) could provide all the necessary icons. Or, one could imagine some delightful integrated interactions like this one that would make it easy and pleasant to make the Touch Bar feel personally useful.

sentences.en: In a better setup, it would be possible to assign any key or action or menu command to any ground-floor Touch Bar button; something like SF Symbols (formalized in 2019) could provide all the necessary icons.
sentences.zh: 在更好的设置中，可以将任何键或操作或菜单命令分配给任何底层 Touch Bar 按钮；像 SF Symbols（2019 年正式化）这样的东西可以提供所有必要的图标。

sentences.en: Or, one could imagine some delightful integrated interactions like this one that would make it easy and pleasant to make the Touch Bar feel personally useful.
sentences.zh: 或者，人们可以想象一些令人愉快的集成交互，就像这样，它会让 Touch Bar 感觉对个人有用，变得轻松愉快。

blocks.html_en: Or, how about sparklines or other tiny widgets that’d quickly show visual status, of the kind pro users like to put in the menu bar already, and easily pluggable to data sources (see the very recent TerminalWidget)? Or a left/​right slide gesture, buttons, or a keyboard combination to swap between Touch Bar “spaces”?

sentences.en: Or, how about sparklines or other tiny widgets that’d quickly show visual status, of the kind pro users like to put in the menu bar already, and easily pluggable to data sources (see the very recent TerminalWidget)?
sentences.zh: 或者，迷你图或其他可以快速显示视觉状态的小部件怎么样，专业用户喜欢将其放入菜单栏中，并且可以轻松插入数据源（请参阅最近的 TerminalWidget）？

sentences.en: Or a left/​right slide gesture, buttons, or a keyboard combination to swap between Touch Bar “spaces”?
sentences.zh: 或者通过左/右滑动手势、按钮或键盘组合在 Touch Bar“空间”之间切换？

blocks.html_en: How about learning what commands you use most often that don’t have keyboard shortcuts, per app, and suggesting them as the first five buttons on the Touch Bar?

sentences.en: How about learning what commands you use most often that don’t have keyboard shortcuts, per app, and suggesting them as the first five buttons on the Touch Bar?
sentences.zh: 了解每个应用程序中您最常使用哪些没有键盘快捷键的命令，并建议将它们作为触摸栏上的前五个按钮，怎么样？

blocks.html_en: Could the Touch Bar have been saved?

sentences.en: Could the Touch Bar have been saved?
sentences.zh: Touch Bar还有救吗？

blocks.html_en: Today, it often feels like the Touch Bar chose revolution in the moments the right answer was evolution, and evolution in places that called for a revolution. With hindsight, after seeing projects like Stream Deck and Flux Keyboard capture people’s attention, maybe it could have worked this way:

sentences.en: Today, it often feels like the Touch Bar chose revolution in the moments the right answer was evolution, and evolution in places that called for a revolution.
sentences.zh: 如今，人们常常感觉 Touch Bar 在正确答案是进化的时刻选择了革命，并且在需要革命的地方进行了进化。

sentences.en: With hindsight, after seeing projects like Stream Deck and Flux Keyboard capture people’s attention, maybe it could have worked this way:
sentences.zh: 事后看来，在看到像 Stream Deck 和 Flux Keyboard 这样的项目吸引了人们的注意力后，也许它可以这样工作：

blocks.html_en: • First version arrives with a physical Esc or at least “sound-based haptics,” and allows you to do more things via much nicer settings software: easy assigning of buttons to system actions, and icons so you no longer have to remember whether it was F3 or F7 doing your thing. Don’t treat the Touch Bar as repudiation of function keys, but as their enhancement. On top of that, add some easy-to-put-together widgetlets and sparklines. This is Pro hardware, and these feel like pro features.

sentences.en: First version arrives with a physical Esc or at least “sound-based haptics,” and allows you to do more things via much nicer settings software: easy assigning of buttons to system actions, and icons so you no longer have to remember whether it was F3 or F7 doing your thing.
sentences.zh: 第一个版本带有物理 Esc 或至少“基于声音的触觉”，并允许您通过更好的设置软件做更多事情：轻松地将按钮分配给系统操作和图标，这样您就不再需要记住是 F3 还是 F7 在做您的事情。

sentences.en: Don’t treat the Touch Bar as repudiation of function keys, but as their enhancement.
sentences.zh: 不要将 Touch Bar 视为对功能键的否定，而应将其视为功能键的增强。

sentences.en: On top of that, add some easy-to-put-together widgetlets and sparklines.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，添加一些易于组合的小部件和迷你图。

sentences.en: This is Pro hardware, and these feel like pro features.
sentences.zh: 这是专业硬件，这些感觉就像专业功能。

blocks.html_en: • Staying tighter, focused, and reigning in some more complex interactions would help, too (problem: they look so good in videos!). Instead of boiling the ocean and recreating a lot of the existing GUI in a cramped space, focus on just one–two great interactions per app. Finder: Show the Quick Actions that were already customizable and not as easy to access in some views! Emoji: Paginate instead of scroll, but do a really clever pagination that highlights the power of a parallax swipe gesture that can only exist here. System: Add immediate screenshotting by default.

sentences.en: Staying tighter, focused, and reigning in some more complex interactions would help, too (problem: they look so good in videos!).
sentences.zh: 保持更紧密、专注，并控制一些更复杂的互动也会有所帮助（问题：它们在视频中看起来很棒！）。

sentences.en: Instead of boiling the ocean and recreating a lot of the existing GUI in a cramped space, focus on just one–two great interactions per app.
sentences.zh: 与其在狭窄的空间中煮沸海洋并重新创建大量现有的 GUI，不如只专注于每个应用程序的一到两个出色的交互。

sentences.en: Finder: Show the Quick Actions that were already customizable and not as easy to access in some views!
sentences.zh: Finder：显示已经可自定义但在某些视图中不太容易访问的快速操作！

sentences.en: Emoji: Paginate instead of scroll, but do a really clever pagination that highlights the power of a parallax swipe gesture that can only exist here.
sentences.zh: 表情符号：分页而不是滚动，但进行了非常巧妙的分页，突出了只能存在于此处的视差滑动手势的力量。

sentences.en: System: Add immediate screenshotting by default.
sentences.zh: 系统：默认添加立即截图。

blocks.html_en: • If this worked, subsequent versions would add haptics, perhaps increase the size, and go mainstream from pro users to regular users, learning all the useful lessons along the way (also from third-party apps like Pock).

sentences.en: If this worked, subsequent versions would add haptics, perhaps increase the size, and go mainstream from pro users to regular users, learning all the useful lessons along the way (also from third-party apps like Pock).
sentences.zh: 如果这有效，后续版本将添加触觉，也许会增加尺寸，并从专业用户到普通用户成为主流，并在此过程中学习所有有用的经验教训（也来自 Pock 等第三方应用程序）。

blocks.html_en: But I’m not sure. Touch is fun but there is, ultimately, a ceiling on value you can squeeze out of a small touch strip, and a floor on complexity of yet another input/​output device.

sentences.en: But I’m not sure.
sentences.zh: 但我不确定。

sentences.en: Touch is fun but there is, ultimately, a ceiling on value you can squeeze out of a small touch strip, and a floor on complexity of yet another input/​output device.
sentences.zh: 触摸很有趣，但最终，你可以从一个小触摸条中挤出的价值上限，以及另一个输入/输出设备的复杂性下限。

blocks.html_en: And there was always an elephant in the hardware room – many pro users are likely to use computers on desks with separate keyboards, which puts the Touch Bar either too far away or makes it altogether inaccessible. In the decade since, Apple hasn’t even solved this for Touch ID, the only part of the Touch Bar that didn’t get sacrificed to the angry IBM 3270 terminal gods.

sentences.en: And there was always an elephant in the hardware room – many pro users are likely to use computers on desks with separate keyboards, which puts the Touch Bar either too far away or makes it altogether inaccessible.
sentences.zh: 硬件室里总是有大象——许多专业用户可能会在带有独立键盘的办公桌上使用计算机，这使得 Touch Bar 要么太远，要么完全无法访问。

sentences.en: In the decade since, Apple hasn’t even solved this for Touch ID, the only part of the Touch Bar that didn’t get sacrificed to the angry IBM 3270 terminal gods.
sentences.zh: 此后的十年里，苹果甚至还没有解决 Touch ID 的问题，这是 Touch Bar 中唯一没有被愤怒的 IBM 3270 终端之神牺牲的部分。

blocks.html_en: Would the Touch Bar have worked as a standalone device? Could it ever become good enough for you to want to pay for it twice?

content_html_zh:
Touch Bar 于 2016 年问世，似乎已经注定了它的命运，这一代机器周围弥漫着“我们已经没有创意了”的味道。 方向键被重新设计，键盘被瘦身，甚至连人们喜爱的 MagSafe 事实上也并不安全。 所有这些改变最终都会被证明是不受欢迎的，并会及时恢复，最终 Touch Bar 也会被砍掉。

事后看来，在它问世十年后，在（传闻中的）全多点触控 MacBook 出现的前夕，我想更详细地批判性地审视 Touch Bar。 我在这篇文章上面放了一个辛辣的标题，虽然我不确定我能给出肯定的回答，但我觉得我已经非常接近了。

Touch Bar 做了什么？

Touch Bar 用狭窄的触摸屏和右侧的 Touch ID 表面/按钮取代了键盘的顶行。

触摸屏在左侧提供了一个恒定的虚拟 Esc 键，其余部分可能会成为以下几项之一：

  • 应用程序控件 – 应用程序想要的任何内容（按钮或更具交互性的界面）：
  • 控制条 – 与当今功能键的默认功能大致相同（亮度、传输控制、音量）：
  • 左侧较小应用程序控件和右侧可扩展控制条的混合模式：
  • F1–F12 键：
  • 一些较小的模式，例如显示空间、快速操作或表情符号：
  • 小子模式，其中仅触摸栏的中间将被接管：

The Verge 有一个五分钟的视频，很好地展示了很多这样的东西。

功能性

Touch Bar 为休闲用户和专业用户提供了混合功能 - 有些内置于 macOS 本身，有些来自特定的 Apple 自有应用程序。

一些应用程序基本上提供了工具栏的子集（尽管通常没有自定义），偶尔还会有子菜单，例如深入研究字体选项或选择颜色调整。 Safari 和 Photo 等一些应用程序会投资于对象的微小预览。

特别适合演示的是音量和亮度的滑块，以及特定应用程序中的滑块——在 QuickTime 中播放，或在照片库中滑动，显然受到 iPhone 上类似控件的启发。 尽管 Touch Bar 被称为“多点触控”，但它实际上只支持点击和水平滑动，而后者是经典功能键显然无法做到的。

一个简单但有效的方法是指向 Touch ID 授权和支付的箭头——软件本体感知的一个小例子——苹果甚至将其作为 GIF 包含在其新闻稿中：

但也有一些奇怪的时刻，这个策略感觉有点像“让我们投入很多东西，看看什么能坚持下去”（话又说回来，它适用于第一代 Apple Watch！）：

  • 任何系统对话框都会在触摸栏中重复显示其按钮。 这让我感到困惑，因为鼠标交互和键盘（Esc/Enter）已经很好地服务了这些。
  • 很高兴你可以拖动音量或亮度控制，但随后滑块会与你的手指断开连接，并且音量也会出现在屏幕上的旧HUD中，总感觉系统的不同部分彼此不知道。
  • Xcode 提供了一个按钮来注释当前行或选择，这对程序员来说肯定是一种侮辱——有没有人更喜欢这个而不是 ⌘/ 组合键？

最后，对于第一版，IA 感觉很复杂：

  • 单词补全位于栏的中间，但表情符号入口点位于左侧。
  • V 形有很多种（至少三种！），而且其动作与箭头并不完全匹配 - 有些 V 形确实使控件朝预期方向扩展，但有些反而钻得更深并占据了一半的条形，而另一些则接管了整个操作。 （最重要的是，一些控件有常规的水平滚动。）
  • 一些看起来像常规按钮的控件也会在点击时展开，因此实际上从来没有真正清楚触摸时控件会做什么。
  • 关闭框有时位于按钮的左侧，有时位于按钮的右侧。
设置

奇怪的是，对于如此引人注目的功能，触摸栏设置散落在旧键盘选项之间，而不是在单独的触摸栏选项卡中，这样可以帮助您更轻松地了解整个系统，并且还可以提供对可能功能的良好预览。

苹果对品牌的偏爱，即使是小东西，也产生了一点适得其反的效果——定制 Touch Bar 需要面对一些奇怪的短语，比如“快速操作”、“应用程序控制”和“控制条”（这就是通常不怀旧的苹果重复使用经典名称的地方，而不是将其命名为“系统控制”以反映应用程序控制）。

另一方面，这里的自定义控制条交互绝对是一大亮点，它在 Touch Bar 的世界和上方的天空之间提供了一座神奇的桥梁——这可能是整个系统中设计得最好的部分：

（这种自定义功能在某些支持 Touch Bar 的应用程序中也可用，但并非所有应用程序都可用。） 顺便说一句，苹果自 2016 年以来似乎已经吸取了设置教训，甚至学得过头了； 2023 年 iPhone 引入的操作按钮配备了华丽的新界面：

最初的公众反应和演变

早在 2016 年，Touch Bar 的出现就带来了一种温和的乐观情绪（“不太好，也许很有希望，期待第二季和第三季”），但似乎每个依赖物理 Esc 键的人都表示强烈的挫败感。 Touch Bar 只在 2019 年被重新审视过一次；这次轻微的更新重新引入了机械 Esc 键，使用起来感觉稍快一些。

没有其他硬件改进，我相信苹果在该功能的整个生命周期内软件变化为零。 一些第三方应用程序在最初几年添加了 Touch Bar 支持，但即便如此，结论似乎还是有些保留：

大多数 Final Cut Pro 高级用户将习惯于使用键盘快捷键来执行他们经常使用的编辑功能，以至于他们可能无法更快地找到 Touch Bar 来进行简单的编辑和播放，但与上下文相关的设置的数量之多意味着它最终可能会证明其价值。

Touch Bar 从未出现在非 Pro MacBook 或其他电脑上，并在推出五年后开始被完全淘汰。 令人困惑的是，出于我们可能永远不知道的原因，该项目几乎在启动后就得到了“维护”，并且没有立即删除，也许只是为了保全面子。

触觉和人体工程学

Touch Bar 的手指感觉不舒服。

人们对 Esc 键的愤怒主要在于它与其他键相比感觉“死气沉沉”，这对于外围的某些东西尤其重要，用作逃生舱口或程序员的核心交互。 （按键也略有偏移，可能只是为了与另一侧的 Touch ID 保持对称。）

我敢打赌，触摸栏按钮的感觉与下面的真实按键的感觉不可避免地不断进行比较，这使得整个事情感觉比实际更糟糕，而且我一直想知道触觉是否可以在这里提供帮助。 如果轻触可提供温和的触觉反馈，类似于无需按下按键即可感觉到按键的“脊”，而更深的按压可提供适当的触觉敲击，结果会怎样呢？

早在 2016 年，苹果就在触控板下方采用了类似的技术。 我敢打赌，我低估了重新调整它的用途的难度和成本，但是：iPod 从来没有真正的触觉反馈，但即使在第一个模型中，它们也带有一个小扬声器，可以在操作时发出类似触觉的声音。 它出奇地有效，我很好奇为什么苹果没有在这里做同样的事情。

最重要的是，虽然上面的一排功能键对于偶尔按下来说很有趣，但从人体工程学角度来看，长时间使用它似乎并不那么好。 无论您将其放在下方还是侧面，触碰触控栏都比触碰触控板更费力——键盘变宽是有原因的，但很少会变高。 在上面的 The Verge 视频中，您可以看到审阅者在与下面的触控板交互时使用 Touch Bar 按钮作为修饰键，光是看着这种情况就感觉不舒服：

最重要的是，Touch Bar 的表面低于按键的表面，这使得使用起来稍微不太舒服——它不仅感觉像是在按键上方，而且还感觉在按键后面。

还有其他一些粗糙的边缘：

  • Touch Bar 会急切地进入睡眠状态（仅 60+15 秒后），隐藏其所有控件并迫使您点击它或按某个键将其唤醒。
  • 动画的质量与其他触摸设备或 Apple TV 上的不同。
  • 虽然 Touch Bar 本身的速度足以支持平滑滚动，但按下 Fn 键和某些 Touch Bar 控件时也会出现一些（我认为是故意的）延迟，而且每次触摸时都会出现轻微但可察觉的延迟。
  • 说到滚动，它是不平衡的：在日历中，你可以使用动量滚动，但日历不会实时更新，并且通过点击任意位置来停止动量，就像在 iPhone 上实际上选择了不同的月份一样：
  • 通常，退出子模式的唯一方法是按左侧的关闭框，考虑到你手的位置，这很不愉快；没有深思熟虑的捷径，比如双击一个选项，可以更快地退出。
Size

使用 Touch Bar 时要不断意识到它的小尺寸：预览很小，手指始终与内容重叠，并且滚动仅发生在水平面上。 （而且你的手指必须保持在一条直线上，而不是轻微的弧线——这不是一个自然的手势。）

扩展控制条需要点击一个非常小的 V 形；其他地方也有大量这样的小 V 形图案，它们很窄，如果没有触觉反馈，很难按下。 它让界面感觉很繁琐，这是一家公司的奇怪妥协，该公司在第一代 iPhone 上深思熟虑地制定并强制执行了“44 像素”最小触摸目标尺寸。 （V 形图案正好是 2007 年 iPhone 上任何触摸目标建议最小物理宽度的一半——3.5 毫米，而不是 7 毫米。）

许多空间在其他方面也感觉紧张。 Craig Federighi 的主题演示展示了 Safari 预览，只有五个选项卡，让人感到幽闭恐怖：

使用任何打字表面时，触摸栏将分为三个区域：应用程序控件、建议单词和右侧的控制条：

在其他应用程序中，某些区域是可滚动的，但没有空间放置滚动条。 以任何有意义的方式使用 Touch Bar 感觉就像不断猜测什么是可移动的、什么是不可移动的，并不断调整微小的虚拟窗口的大小，除了苹果大屏幕没有任何令人愉快的调整大小机制。 在这里，表情符号窗格 UI 正在做一些非常聪明的事情来帮助遍历数百个表情符号，但它仍然感觉不够：

照片编辑和其他一些地方的交互感觉如此狭窄和复杂，我想知道为什么有人会选择它们而不是上面屏幕的宽敞和精确。

我想知道有限的高度是否还会产生其他下游影响。 例如，向下钻取会产生（缓慢的）淡出/淡出效果，而不是向下和向上滚动来帮助您理解层次结构 - 并显示 V 形符号也指向该方向。 我猜这是因为这个动作会建议你可以上下滑动，但根本没有足够的空间让这个手势感觉良好。

使用 Touch Bar，我不断想起我提到的美妙的自定义功能，该功能巧妙地将 Touch Bar 与上面的屏幕融合在一起，以及 20 世纪 80 年代 Xerox 机器的类似交互（按下面的“更多”键会显示其他选项）：

这是否适用于其他 Touch Bar 交互以创造更多空间，还是会因为您的手指自然地想要点击屏幕底部而变得令人沮丧？ 在文本编辑中，有一个像这样深思熟虑的小集成，触摸栏似乎意识到，当你的手指在楼下时，你可能正在向上看：

但是，在同一个地方，选择颜色的集成方式并不相同：

总而言之，Touch Bar 是一个夹在旧 O 和更旧 I 之间的新 I/O，而且似乎这里的所有关系都没有完全弄清楚。

Touch Bar 会变得更大吗？ 华硕 Zenbook Pro 展示了这个想法的最终结果——它实现了一些新的有趣的事情，但也带来了更多的挑战，比如缺少触控板，或者决定在每个表面上放置什么：

我没想到 Touch Bar 会走得那么远，但我很好奇它会垂直增长一点，以减轻一些痛苦。

定制和基础设施

苹果将​​ Touch Bar 的赌注押在了单个应用程序的内置支持和一些核心交互上。 但事后我想知道答案是否是用户定制。

在这方面，Touch Bar 暴露了苹果在操作基础设施方面投资不足。 macOS 中的键盘自定义在 2016 年就已经显得过时了，此后就没有改进，而且当时甚至还不存在快捷方式应用程序。 这是苹果为大众提供更温和的键盘大师般的体验的机会，但 Touch Bar 不允许你在新功能旁边插入哪怕几个功能键 - 唯一的选择是 F1-F12 的老式模式，没有 Touch Bar 的任何好处（你甚至无法更改标签！），也没有触觉。

当然，快速行动在这个方向上有一个手势，但那些感觉非常不成熟；在我对 Automator 和 Touch Bar 的探索中，我遇到了一些真正令人困惑的设置和流程，并且永远无法使其完全正常工作。 在这里，我必须转到一个遥远的“系统偏好设置”窗格，并查看各种不互相通信的快速操作：

在更好的设置中，可以将任何键或操作或菜单命令分配给任何底层 Touch Bar 按钮；像 SF Symbols（2019 年正式化）这样的东西可以提供所有必要的图标。 或者，人们可以想象一些令人愉快的集成交互，就像这样，它会让 Touch Bar 感觉对个人有用，变得轻松愉快。

或者，迷你图或其他可以快速显示视觉状态的小部件怎么样，专业用户喜欢将其放入菜单栏中，并且可以轻松插入数据源（请参阅最近的 TerminalWidget）？ 或者通过左/右滑动手势、按钮或键盘组合在 Touch Bar“空间”之间切换？

了解每个应用程序中您最常使用哪些没有键盘快捷键的命令，并建议将它们作为触摸栏上的前五个按钮，怎么样？

Touch Bar还有救吗？

如今，人们常常感觉 Touch Bar 在正确答案是进化的时刻选择了革命，并且在需要革命的地方进行了进化。 事后看来，在看到像 Stream Deck 和 Flux Keyboard 这样的项目吸引了人们的注意力后，也许它可以这样工作：

  • 第一个版本带有物理 Esc 或至少“基于声音的触觉”，并允许您通过更好的设置软件做更多事情：轻松地将按钮分配给系统操作和图标，这样您就不再需要记住是 F3 还是 F7 在做您的事情。 不要将 Touch Bar 视为对功能键的否定，而应将其视为功能键的增强。 最重要的是，添加一些易于组合的小部件和迷你图。 这是专业硬件，这些感觉就像专业功能。
  • 保持更紧密、专注，并控制一些更复杂的互动也会有所帮助（问题：它们在视频中看起来很棒！）。 与其在狭窄的空间中煮沸海洋并重新创建大量现有的 GUI，不如只专注于每个应用程序的一到两个出色的交互。 Finder：显示已经可自定义但在某些视图中不太容易访问的快速操作！ 表情符号：分页而不是滚动，但进行了非常巧妙的分页，突出了只能存在于此处的视差滑动手势的力量。 系统：默认添加立即截图。
  • 如果这有效，后续版本将添加触觉，也许会增加尺寸，并从专业用户到普通用户成为主流，并在此过程中学习所有有用的经验教训（也来自 Pock 等第三方应用程序）。

但我不确定。 触摸很有趣，但最终，你可以从一个小触摸条中挤出的价值上限，以及另一个输入/输出设备的复杂性下限。

硬件室里总是有大象——许多专业用户可能会在带有独立键盘的办公桌上使用计算机，这使得 Touch Bar 要么太远，要么完全无法访问。 此后的十年里，苹果甚至还没有解决 Touch ID 的问题，这是 Touch Bar 中唯一没有被愤怒的 IBM 3270 终端之神牺牲的部分。

Touch Bar 可以作为独立设备使用吗？ 它是否会变得足够好，让你愿意为它付两次钱？

也许不是。 但是，如果苹果改进了 Touch Bar 的键盘和动作定制软件，却发现它崩溃了，我们至少仍然可以保留该软件。
